title: Upgrade vsss-rs from 4.3.8 to 5.4.0
description:
Upgrade the `vsss-rs` dependency from 4.3.8 to 5.4.0 (latest published).

## Background

`frozenkrill-core` uses `vsss-rs` for the Pedersen Verifiable Secret Sharing
core that powers the new `split-secret`/`combine-secret` commands. The 5.x
line is a breaking API rewrite — the upgrade isn't just a Cargo.toml bump.

## API changes 4.x → 5.x

| Surface | v4 (current) | v5 (target) |
|---|---|---|
| Share data type | `Vec<u8>` (raw bytes; first byte = share identifier) | `DefaultShare<IdentifierPrimeField<WrappedScalar>, IdentifierPrimeField<WrappedScalar>>` (typed scalar + typed identifier) |
| `StdPedersenResult` type params | `<G, Id, Share>` (3 params) | `<S, V>` (2 params) |
| `pedersen::split_secret` secret arg | by value | by reference (`&S::Value`) |
| `combine_shares` | free function in `vsss_rs::` | now `result.combine()` method on the result |
| Share identifier extraction | `share_bytes[0]` | typed `IdentifierPrimeField<WrappedScalar>` field on the share |
| Verifier set | `vsss_rs::PedersenVerifierSet` trait | `pedersen::Pedersen` re-export + restructured trait surface |

## Files to change

Primary site (only one file in src actually imports vsss-rs):
- `frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs` — touches `vsss_rs::curve25519::{WrappedRistretto, WrappedScalar}`,
  `vsss_rs::pedersen::{StdPedersenResult, split_secret}`, and
  `vsss_rs::{PedersenResult, PedersenVerifierSet, combine_shares}`. Specifically:
  - `split_one_scalar` (the StdPedersenResult call site)
  - `combine_one_half` (the `combine_shares` call site)
  - `verified_unique_share_pairs` (verifier-vec / `verify_share_and_blinder` calls)
  - `parse_ristretto_points` (verifier hex parser)
  - All of the candidate-cross-product enumeration in `combine_vss_wallets`
    that depends on `share_bytes[0]` being the identifier byte
- `frozenkrill-core/Cargo.toml` — `vsss-rs = { version = "5", features = ["curve25519"] }`

## On-disk format implications

Our share files persist `share_data` and `blinder_share_data` as
hex-encoded bytes, currently the raw byte format vsss-rs 4.x emits. v5
serializes typed scalars differently. This is a one-time on-disk format
break — acceptable because the secret-sharing feature has not been
released yet (it's still the open PR #33 against `master`, no users have
committed share files yet).

The `verification_data` (Pedersen verifier set as comma-separated hex of
compressed Ristretto points) MAY be unchanged since Ristretto compression
is a well-established encoding — verify this during the migration rather
than assuming.

## Identifier extraction — careful migration

Several invariants in the codex-hardened combine path key off
`secret_share[0]` being the share identifier byte:
- `verified_unique_share_pairs` dedupe (lines ~556-583)
- The candidate-cross-product enumeration in `combine_vss_wallets` (lines ~882-940)
- HH-2 / II-2 metadata-vote dedupe via 'cryptographic share identifier (first byte of share_data)'

These all need to be rewritten to use v5's typed identifier instead.
The semantics should be preserved (dedupe by share identifier, refuse
ties), but the byte-level access goes away.

## Test surface

The `secret_sharing` test module has 30+ tests covering:
- Round-trip correctness (12-word and 24-word)
- Tampered-share rejection (Pedersen-verification negative cases)
- Per-share verifier corruption tolerance
- Mixed lo/hi verifier corruption (cross-product candidate enumeration)
- Metadata-tamper guards (xpub mismatch, downgrade attacks)
- Duress-mode aggregation
- All of these must continue to pass. Several that currently construct
  `Share` values directly (or compare share_data hex against expected
  byte patterns) may need adaptation to the new types.

## Acceptance criteria

- `vsss-rs = "5"` in `frozenkrill-core/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo build` clean (workspace)
- `cargo test --workspace` green — all existing secret_sharing tests pass
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- The cryptographic semantics are preserved:
  - Same curve (Curve25519/Ristretto via `vsss_rs::curve25519::WrappedRistretto`/`WrappedScalar`)
  - Same Pedersen blind verification (`g^a · h^b` commitments, `verify_share_and_blinder`-equivalent check)
  - Same threshold-secret-sharing behavior
- The on-disk `share_data`/`blinder_share_data` hex format change is
  documented inline in `secret_sharing.rs` (the format is now version-tied
  to vsss-rs 5.x)
- All codex-hardened invariants still hold (per-share dedupe by
  cryptographic identifier, fail-closed metadata authentication,
  candidate cross-product enumeration for split lo/hi corruption, etc.)

## Out of scope

- Bumping `rand`/`rand_core` to 0.9 — separate concern; vsss-rs 5.x still
  pins `rand_core = "0.6"` on its main branch, so this upgrade doesn't
  unblock the rand bump.
- Bumping `bip39` past `>=0.6, <0.9` cap — same reason.
- Refactoring the surrounding wallet_description / share-encryption /
  CLI code beyond what's necessary to fit the new vsss-rs types.

Source: follow-up to PR #33 cleanup; user asked for the vsss bump after
the codex-review-loop converged on v4.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 7c6c6a6 (douglaz/frozenkrill#1, squash-merged into feature/pedersen-secret-sharing). Migrated frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs to vsss-rs 5.4.0's typed Share/Identifier API; updated Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; added flake.nix packages.default for the nix build gate. Validated: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (80 passed), nix build. Implemented via ralph-burning iterative_minimal flow (4 rounds; amendments converged 1→1→2→0).

title: Simplify secret_sharing.rs (collapse Share regroup, gate checksum to tests, unify verifier check, trim comments)
description:
Codex simplification review identified four overlapping refactors all
inside `frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs`. Land them together
because they touch the same recovery path.

## Findings to fix

### 1. Combine candidates directly instead of cloning `Share`s (~150-200 lines)
`combine_vss_wallets` (lines ~1150-1154 in the pre-vsss5 layout) iterates
one verifier candidate at a time, but still clones every input wallet
into a synthetic `Share` so `combine_shares_to_mnemonic` can regroup
them by those same verifier strings. Fold that helper into a candidate-
specific combine over `VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0` directly. Behavior
must be identical; we're just dropping the cloning round-trip.

### 2. Remove test-only `Share` checksum from production flow (~60-80 lines)
The internal `Share::checksum` field and `compute_checksum()` method
are only exercised by tests now. Production split/combine still carries
the field and recomputes it for synthetic shares built during recovery.
Either:
- Gate `checksum` field + `compute_checksum`/`verify_checksum` behind
  `#[cfg(test)]`, OR
- Drop the field entirely and adapt the few tests that assert on it
  to go through the AEAD-backed `VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0` path
  instead.

Prefer the drop-entirely option if the test surface is small enough.

### 3. Single verifier-check helper across recovery paths (~40-60 lines)
The `verifies_lo` / `verifies_hi` closures inside `combine_vss_wallets`
(lines ~1183-1186 pre-vsss5) repeat the hex-decode + share-pair
verification work that `derive_metadata` re-implements a few lines
later. Extract `wallet_verifies_against_candidate(...)` (or similar)
and have both call sites use it. One helper, one place to change the
acceptance rules.

### 4. Trim Pedersen/Shamir tutorial text (a few hundred lines)
`secret_sharing.rs` opens with a tutorial-style module preface and
repeats 10-20 line threat-model explanations beside many individual
branches. Most of the long-form rationale is now duplicated in
`docs/secret_sharing.md` (added during the codex hardening loop).
Trim the inline comments to short intent statements ("Why we abstain
on tied votes"), and lean on the doc for the security narrative.

DO NOT delete comments that:
- Document a non-obvious invariant the code itself doesn't show
  (e.g. "the first byte of share_data IS the share identifier" — but
  with vsss-rs 5.x's typed identifiers, even some of those are now
  obsolete).
- Explain WHY a particular fail-closed branch was added (the codex-
  loop letter-tagged findings — EE-1, FF-2, GG-1, etc. — preserved
  the WHY, and that's load-bearing context for future readers).

DO trim:
- Multi-paragraph threat-model walkthroughs that just restate the
  Pedersen / Shamir definitions.
- Repeated "this is hardened against X" notes when the test suite
  + docs already make X explicit.
- Bullet-list explanations longer than the code they annotate.

## Acceptance criteria

- All existing tests in `frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs::tests`
  still pass (currently 68+ tests after vsss-rs 5.x migration).
- `cargo build --workspace` clean
- `cargo test --workspace` green
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `nix build` passes
- Net line reduction in `frozenkrill-core/src/secret_sharing.rs`
  of at least 250 lines (the four findings combined, conservative
  lower bound).
- All cryptographic semantics preserved — same Pedersen verification,
  same threshold reconstruction, same fail-closed authentication.

## Out of scope (will be a separate bead)

- Dropping `OriginalWalletJson` tagged enum in `wallet_description.rs`.
- Unifying the VSS encryption envelope with the singlesig/multisig
  encoder helpers in `lib.rs`.

Source: codex simplification review of feature/pedersen-secret-sharing
vs origin/master (post-vsss-5 upgrade).

title: Drop OriginalWalletJson enum + unify VSS encryption envelope
description:
Two cross-file API simplifications from the codex simplification review.
They touch `wallet_description.rs` and `lib.rs` (and propagate through
`secret_sharing.rs` callers). Land together as a single follow-up
bead after the secret_sharing.rs internal cleanup lands.

## Findings to fix

### 1. Store singlesig metadata directly in VSS shares (~70-100 lines)
`VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0::original_wallet` is currently typed
`OriginalWalletJson` (a tagged enum: `Singlesig(SinglesigPublicMetadataV0)`
| `Multisig(...)`). But every VSS share in this branch is created by
`split_singlesig_wallet`, and recovery only ever consumes
`SinglesigPublicMetadataV0`. The enum is speculative generality.

Change the field to `original_wallet: SinglesigPublicMetadataV0`
directly. Removes:
- The `OriginalWalletJson` enum definition.
- `is_singlesig` / `is_multisig` helpers.
- Defensive `Multisig` match arms in `to_singlesig` / `derive_metadata`
  (and a couple of similar sites — search the codebase).

If/when a real multisig share format ever needs to be added later,
re-introduce the enum at that point; do not pre-design for it now.

### 2. Reuse standard wallet encryption envelope for VSS (~50-70 lines)
`generate_encrypted_encoded_vss_wallet` in `frozenkrill-core/src/lib.rs`
(lines ~397-405) is effectively a third copy of the same envelope:
serialize → compress → encrypt → header → pad → serialize. The
singlesig and multisig `generate_encrypted_encoded_*` functions
already do this same dance.

Extract a helper (e.g. `encrypt_with_standard_envelope<T: Serialize>(...)`)
and have all three call sites use it. Reduces drift when the encrypted
header / padding rules change later.

The trade-off is one generic helper signature, which is still simpler
than maintaining three near-identical crypto wrappers.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo build --workspace` clean
- `cargo test --workspace` green — every existing test passes,
  including all share round-trip tests and the encryption envelope
  tests
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `nix build` passes
- Net line reduction across `wallet_description.rs` and `lib.rs`
  of at least 100 lines combined.
- Cryptographic / on-disk format semantics unchanged: encryption
  envelope structure, header bytes, padding rules — all identical
  before and after.
- The on-disk JSON layout of `VssJsonWalletDescriptionV0` may simplify
  (the `original_wallet` field's tag / variant wrapping goes away),
  but this is acceptable because the secret-sharing feature has not
  been released yet (still PR #33 against master).

## Out of scope

- Anything in `secret_sharing.rs` (handled by the previous bead).
- Adding multisig support — the simplification is precisely about
  not building speculative multisig infrastructure.

Source: codex simplification review of feature/pedersen-secret-sharing
vs origin/master (post-vsss-5 upgrade).
